## 1. SKILLS CATALOG

**Purpose:** Live list of skills with everything the model needs for correct arbitration, activation, and `execute_skill` decisions.

Skills appear in descending arbitration priority (highest influence first).

### create-skill
**Description:** Interactively create a new Grok skill (SKILL.md + optional scripts/references). Use when the user wants to create a skill, scaffold a skill, or runs /create-skill.
**Arbitration Score:** 50 (higher = appears earlier / stronger influence)
**When to prefer / activate this skill:**
- Match the description and triggers above.
- Call with `execute_skill "create-skill" "user input here"` or activate via `/activate create-skill`.

### skill-builder
**Description:** Dynamic skill creation system - builds, validates, and activates custom skills on-the-fly from specifications or natural language
**Arbitration Score:** 50 (higher = appears earlier / stronger influence)
**Tags:** meta-skill, skill-creation, automation, development
**When to prefer / activate this skill:**
- Match the description and triggers above.
- Call with `execute_skill "skill-builder" "user input here"` or activate via `/activate skill-builder`.

<!-- HOOKS SECTION START -->
## 2. HOOKS

**Purpose:** Automatic logic that runs around tool calls. The model should **rely on hooks** instead of re-implementing the same behavior.

### Hook Types

**before_tool**
- Executes before any tool call.
- Can block the call or add context.
- Common uses: security policy, logging, auto-approval, input sanitization.

**after_tool**
- Executes after tool completion.
- Receives tool name + result.
- Common uses: post-processing, auditing, triggering side effects.

### Guidance for the Model
- Trust that `before_tool` / `after_tool` will run when `tools.enable_hooks = true`.
- Do not duplicate hook logic (e.g. don't manually add safety checks a hook already performs).
- If a tool is blocked by a hook, the response will usually explain why.
- Prefer relying on existing hooks over writing new custom code in skills.

<!-- HOOKS SECTION END -->

<!-- OPTIMIZATION HEURISTICS START -->
## 3. OPTIMIZATION HEURISTICS

**Purpose:** Concrete patterns the model should prefer to reduce latency, allocations, token usage, and tool-loop iterations.

### Skill & Tool Usage
- Prefer `execute_skill "name"` over re-implementing the same logic with many primitive tool calls.
- Activate relevant skills early (see Skills Catalog) instead of doing general reasoning.
- Use ranked skill context (higher arbitration scores first) rather than dumping everything.

### History & Message Construction (cheap clones)
- Use `Arc<str>` for message content (already done in ConversationItem).
- Avoid full history clones on every turn — prefer bounded windows + `std::mem::take`.
- Keep static prompt fragments and tool schemas cached.

### Prompt Building
- Use `String::with_capacity` + `push_str` instead of repeated `format!` where hot.
- Prefer single owned values for system messages when possible.

### General Performance Rules
- When `GROK_PERF=1` is set, pay attention to the reported per-turn timings.
- In ACP/sub-agent paths, minimize time spent holding locks.
- For interactive suggestions and UI, use `LazyLock` / statics (already applied to many suggestion lists).

**Primary Goal:** Fewer tool-loop iterations + lower per-turn memory allocations.

<!-- OPTIMIZATION HEURISTICS END -->
